messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging evan-oncall (on-call) — amberwave-financial (VPC ap-southeast1) p99 latency spike detected on dedicated pool 'aw-pool-03'. Current p99 12.8s (SLO 3s). Impacting API endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Autoscale did not add nodes in last 15m.
evan-oncall: ack — looking. any customer contact?
julie-customer-success: Julie here, AmberWave is on call too. They reported increased error/latency since ~04:10 UTC. Business impact: payment reconciliation timeouts for some merchants. They asked for progress updates.
evan-oncall: got it. first triage: checking pool utilization and recent deploys. @mike-sre can you grab node metrics + recent kernel logs?
mike-sre: on it. pulling GPU util, queue depth, network egress. preliminary: GPU util is low (~10%) but request queue is backed up, lots of retries from edge LB. suspect KV cache thrash or hot-tenant storm.
ashley-platform: no deploys in last hour. config for aw-pool-03 unchanged. Batching config still default for the tenant.
\tony-network: checking fabric — no region-wide networking incident. egress for ap-southeast1 to customer VPC looks healthy but we see elevated retransmits to 10.1.32.0/24 (amberwave subnets).
evan-oncall: good. Mike, can you sample request traces and show top 10 tenants by qps?
mike-sre: copying traces -> top tenant by qps is amberwave-tenant (x6 baseline), but I also see a surge of many small 1-token requests from telemetry third-party in same VPC. queue depth per-gpu: 850 -> 300ms avg scheduling latency -> queuing p99 high.
sara-eng: if amberwave tenant is hot and generating many tiny requests, batching can be inefficient. Consider enforcing per-tenant queue cap and moving noisy tenants to isolation.
evan-oncall: plan: 1) Enable tenant isolation (drain noisy telemetry subnet) 2) Expand pool (add 2 warm nodes) 3) Route amberwave traffic to dedicated warm spare region (apse1->apse2 fallback) 4) Short-term model fallback to quantized variant for lower p99.
ops-bot: Running playbook 'tenant-isolation-v2' for tenant amberwave-tenant. Approver required: evan-oncall.
evan-oncall: approve ops-bot run.
ops-bot: Isolation job started: creating isolation queue, setting tenant priority=high, throttle=200rps. ETA 40s.
mike-sre: started scale-up: provisioning 2 warm instances in aw-pool-03. provisioning time ~2m.
ashley-platform: routing rule ready: can do traffic split 70/30 amberwave apse1->apse2. need evan approval to flip.
evan-oncall: flip to 70/30 now.
ashley-platform: applied: 70% to ap-southeast2 warm spare, 30% staying ap-southeast1.
julie-customer-success: AmberWave says they see immediate improvement on some endpoints, still seeing p99 ~5s on reconcile flows. They appreciate team communication.
mike-sre: scaling finished. new nodes joined pool; but queue still sticky — looks like KV cache miss storms causing repeated re-evaluation of prefixes.
evan-oncall: try forcing KV cache warm for amberwave prefixes. can we pre-warm keys?
ashley-platform: running kv-prefetch for tenant amberwave-tenant across new nodes.
ashley-platform: pre-warm done.
mike-sre: cache hit ratio improved from 12% -> 72%. request latency p95 down to 1.2s, p99 3.8s. We still see occasional spikes tied to external telemetry requests in same VPC.
sara-eng: short-term mitigation: add per-tenant request caps on telemetry clients and route them to a throttled queue. Longer-term: shard KV namespace by tenant and enforce stricter cache isolation.
evan-oncall: apply telemetry cap now.
ops-bot: applied throttle rule for telemetry clients in AmberWave VPC: max concurrency 50.
mike-sre: after throttle, p99 is 2.6s. still above SLO but substantially better.
julie-customer-success: AmberWave PM asks for timeline to full SLO recovery and whether this will recur.
evan-oncall: short answer: we have steady mitigation path. next steps: continue traffic split to apse2 until p99 < 3s for 15m, keep telemetry caps, and schedule follow-up with AmberWave on root cause.\tony-network: one more note — we saw packet retransmit bursts from an edge NAT on their side at 04:15. I recommend asking AmberWave to check egress NAT health; could be contributing.
julie-customer-success: I'll loop AmberWave infra and ask them to validate NATs and share tcpdump if possible.
nashley-platform: creating a canary route to gradually reduce split: going to 50/50 in 10m if metrics hold.
evan-oncall: agreed. also enable model fallback to 8-bit quantized variant for endpoints /v1/generate for this tenant. low risk but reduces inference time.
ashley-platform: fallback enabled for amberwave-tenant on /v1/generate.
mike-sre: p99 now 1.9s. p95 900ms. metrics trending stable.
sara-eng: capture a replay of the request pattern for postmortem: `curl https://replay.internal/api/recordings/1789998888` and save to /mnt/pm-replay/amberwave-1789998888.tar.gz
evan-oncall: logging this as incident INC-2026-0456. primary mitigations applied: tenant isolation, traffic split to warm spare region, kv pre-warm, telemetry throttle, scale-up, model fallback.\julie-customer-success: AmberWave notified of mitigations and will keep us posted. they requested a formal postmortem and a scheduled follow-up call.\mike-sre: I'll collect traces, kernel logs, and schedule a deep-dive with research team to identify why kv thrash happened.
ops-bot: Runbook step: handoff to next on-call in 2h. Do you want to escalate to on-call rotation?
evan-oncall: yes — will handoff to sara-eng at 1789999402 UTC. leaving amberwave in 50/50 split, telemetry caps in place. monitoring alerts adjusted to p99 > 4s.\sara-eng: taking handoff. will monitor for 30m and then coordinate postmortem.\evan-oncall: thanks team — leaving a short post in #incidents-summary and a note for Customer Success to schedule call.\julie-customer-success: will set up 11:00 APSE1 call and gather their network logs.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0456 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
sara-eng: noted. continuing watch. :eyes:
